subtype: Approach: noticing tiredness and changing the routine [Revision]
passage: The school bus came at 6:40, and Anand had been getting into bed after midnight because of the game. On Tuesday his head dropped in Sharmila Ma'am's class, and he jerked awake to laughter and a page of blank notes. That stung. On the bus home he added it up: sleep lost, notes lost, and he had not even won. By afternoon he had a new plan. He would play from four to five, right after snack, and the console would go into the hall cupboard at nine, before brushing his teeth. The next Tuesday he was awake for the whole lesson and even asked a question.

qa.q: At what time did Anand decide the console would go into the cupboard?
qa.a: He decided it would go in at nine, before brushing his teeth.

qa.q: What was Anand feeling when he woke up to the laughter in class?
qa.a: Embarrassed, since his head dropped and he woke to laughter and a page of blank notes.

qa.q: What else could help Anand besides moving the game?
qa.a: He could keep a fixed bedtime and wind down with a book, because a steady routine helps him wake up ready for the early bus.

qa.q: How might Sharmila Ma'am see Anand's change?
qa.a: With pleasure and some surprise, since he was awake for the whole lesson and even asked a question.

grounding: After falling asleep in class from late gaming, a boy sees the cost and moves the game to the afternoon.

subtype: Approach: noticing tiredness and changing the routine [Revision]
passage: Shankar woke with a jolt to laughter. His cheek was on his maths notebook, and Varun, beside him, was whispering, "Sir's looking at you." The teacher only said, "Late night?", but Shankar's face burned for the rest of the day. He had played his football game till past midnight again. On the bus home he thought about it. "Four nights this week. Four mornings like a zombie." That evening he talked to his father. "Can I play from four-thirty to five-thirty, before tuition, instead of at night?" His father agreed, and Shankar himself suggested the console go on top of the fridge at nine. By the next week he was wide awake in maths, and Varun had to find something else to laugh at.

qa.q: How did Shankar feel after waking up in class?
qa.a: Embarrassed; his face burned for the rest of the day.

qa.q: What else could help Shankar keep the new routine?
qa.a: Keeping the console out of his room at night altogether, so the nine o'clock rule is easy to follow.

qa.q: How might Varun see the change?
qa.a: Varun now has an alert friend beside him in maths instead of a sleepy one to laugh at.

grounding: After falling asleep in class from late gaming, a boy moves his playtime to the afternoon and puts the console away by nine.

subtype: Approach: noticing tiredness and changing the routine [Revision]
passage:
"Pankaj-bhaiya, I fell asleep in science today."
"In class?"
"On the desk. Ma'am woke me up by tapping the duster. Everyone laughed."
"Because you played till one again."
"Twelve-thirty." Lokesh sighed. "I keep saying one more match. I'm tired every morning."
"So what will you do?"
"I was thinking on the way home. If I play after school, from five to six, I'm done before dinner. And the console..." He hesitated. "The console goes in your room at nine. You keep it."
"Me? You'll bang on my door."
"I won't. That's the point. If it's in my room, I'll play."
"Fine. From nine o'clock it's mine till morning."
"And if I ask for it back, don't give it."

qa.q: Until what time did Lokesh play last night?
How did Lokesh feel when everyone laughed?
qa.a: Embarrassed, and fed up with being tired every morning.

qa.q: What else could help Lokesh stick to the plan?
qa.a: Setting an alarm at five to six, so the afternoon session ends without an argument with himself.
He teases a little but agrees to hold the console every night.

grounding: After falling asleep in class from late gaming, a boy moves his playtime to the afternoon and hands over the console at nine.
